question: A 60-year-old smoker has a central hilar mass on CT with biopsy confirming small cell lung cancer (SCLC). Which statement about the management of SCLC is correct?

answers.text: SCLC is almost never resected surgically; chemotherapy (and radiotherapy for limited disease) is the mainstay of treatment because SCLC is nearly always disseminated at diagnosis

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. SCLC is a rapidly proliferating neuroendocrine tumour that is almost always disseminated by the time of diagnosis (only about 5% present as truly localised disease). Surgery is rarely indicated; the mainstay is platinum-based chemotherapy ± thoracic radiotherapy for limited disease, and prophylactic cranial irradiation to prevent brain metastases.

answers.text: Surgical lobectomy is the first-line treatment for SCLC if the tumour is confined to one lobe

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Even apparently localised SCLC carries micrometastatic disease at presentation in the vast majority of cases. Surgery is not the standard approach — the rapid doubling time and early metastatic spread of SCLC mean that systemic chemotherapy is the foundation of treatment.

answers.text: SCLC is primarily treated by surgery, with chemotherapy added only if nodes are positive

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. This is the approach to resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), not SCLC. SCLC is considered a systemic disease at presentation and surgery plays almost no role.

answers.text: SCLC is more amenable to surgical resection than squamous cell carcinoma of the lung because it tends to be central and well-defined

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. The central location and well-demarcated appearance of SCLC does NOT make it more resectable — it is less so, because SCLC invariably has early occult metastases that surgery cannot address.

overallFeedback.feedback: The critical distinction: SCLC = systemic disease → chemotherapy first; NSCLC = surgical resection for stages I-IIIa. SCLC's rapid doubling time and early micrometastases make it almost always non-resectable.
Well done. SCLC is a systemic disease at diagnosis — surgery rarely has a role. Chemotherapy (etoposide + cisplatin/carboplatin) is the cornerstone, with radiotherapy for limited-stage disease.
